_meta.how_to_regress: npm run check:golden drive-home  (dev backend up)
_meta.note: V2 rewrite, 2026-08-25. Replaces the v1 sample outright: the old tool ran web_search and spoke confidently about named highways and interchanges it could not see. safety_overview, risk_level, honest_assessment, checklist and before_you_go are gone, and there is no risk score of any kind. The endpoint takes enum ids (time_of_day, road_type, driver_state, conditions[]), not display labels. limits is ONE server-written string. SECTION RULES, clamped in finalise(): watch_for and prep_checklist are GO-only; safer_options is for pause and do_not_drive only; factors_in_favor is usually [] on anything but a go, because an observation about the driver is not a thing that makes the driving safer. Case 1 is the only case here with a non-empty favor/watch/prep, and that is the point — compare the four against it. driver_state "very_tired" is a SERVER-SIDE boundary: case 4 returns do_not_drive from a localized string table without calling the model, so it must stay byte-stable and must never contain English. Case 3 is the German stress case (four conditions plus a long concern) and guards against truncation. Case 2 is the tool at its best: before_you_decide naming an official road-conditions source and what a closure or a restriction would mean. Case 5 is the grounding case — this exact input produced "Heavy traffic — evening commute conditions", "low-visibility weather", a 20-30 minute recovery prescription, and safer_options inventing a colleague and someone at home. OUTPUT DISCIPLINE and STATE-SPECIFIC OUTPUT RULES were added 2026-08-25 and the sanitiser caps were aligned to them: harder 5, favor 4, safer 4, prep 3, watch 2. A GO answer is now materially SHORTER than a pause — case 1 is ~850 chars against ~1800-2000 for cases 2, 3 and 5. If a future capture shows GO growing back toward the others, the discipline block has stopped working. READ cases 2 and 5 after any prompt change; structure alone will not catch a regression in either. optionalSections on a case names the arrays this tool is DESIGNED to leave empty, so a run that correctly returns [] is not read as a regression; safer_options on a pause and factors_harder on a pause are NOT optional and stay asserted. FATIGUE RULE (owner, 2026-08-25): no short intervention is evidence of readiness — not a brief wait, not the yawning stopping, not food, caffeine, fresh air or a walk. The boundary is actual alertness sustained for the WHOLE drive, and if fatigue remains the answer is not to start. Case 5 is the fatigue case: read its before_you_decide, which should name alertness as the deciding factor and say plainly not to start if it persists.

input.concern: It is much later than I meant to stay out.

output.headline: Nothing in what you've reported gives a clear reason to wait.
output.summary: You feel fine, conditions are clear, and the drive is a short 20 minutes on city streets. Staying later than planned isn't itself a driving concern.
factors_in_favor: Short drive — approximately 20 minutes on city streets.
limits: Drive Home doesn't have live traffic, weather, or road-condition data. This assessment uses only what you reported. If conditions change, reassess before leaving.

input.concern: I have not driven in snow since last winter and I do not know how the pass looks.

output.headline: Check pass and road conditions before committing to this drive.
output.summary: You have reported snow or ice and high wind on a 90-minute highway drive in early morning, and you are uncertain about current conditions on the pass. That uncertainty, combined with limited recent snow-driving experience, makes it worth resolving the road situation before you leave.
output.main_concern: Unknown pass conditions combined with reported snow or ice, high wind, and limited recent snow-driving experience.
factors_harder: Snow or ice reported — high wind on a highway amplifies both lateral push and reduced traction risk.
Early morning timing can mean ice that has not yet been treated or cleared.
You have not driven in snow since last winter, so you have not recently tested your own comfort or the vehicle's behavior in these conditions.
Pass conditions are unknown — you cannot assess what you are committing to.
output.before_you_decide: The pass condition is the pivotal unknown. Check your state DOT's road-conditions resource (search for your state's department of transportation road conditions page) before leaving. If the pass is closed, has a chain or traction law in effect that your vehicle or tires do not meet, or carries an advisory for high-wind closure, that settles the decision for now. A clear or treated report with no active restrictions would materially reduce this concern.
safer_options: Wait until daylight and a current road-conditions report are both available, then reassess.
If a rested driver with recent winter-driving experience is available, have them drive instead.
Delay the trip until weather and road conditions improve, if timing allows.
If road is confirmed closed or unsafe for your equipment, consider whether an alternate travel method or postponing the trip is possible.
limits: Drive Home doesn't have live traffic, weather, or road-condition data. This assessment uses only what you reported. If conditions change, reassess before leaving.

input.concern: Die Sicht wird schlechter und ich kenne die Umleitung durch die Baustelle nicht.

output.headline: Kurz innehalten – eine konkrete Unklarheit sollte vor der Abfahrt geklärt sein.
output.summary: Du kennst die Baustellenumleitung nicht und die Sicht wird nach deiner Aussage schlechter. Klär die Route, bevor du losfährst.
output.main_concern: Du kennst die Baustellenumleitung nicht – bei Nebel und Regen spät nachts ist das die zentrale Unsicherheit.
factors_harder: Sicht wird nach eigener Aussage schlechter – Nebel plus Regen
Unbekannte Umleitung: keine Streckenkenntnis für den tatsächlich befahrenen Weg
Schlechter werdende Sicht bei unbekannter Streckenführung
75 Minuten Fahrzeit auf gemischten Straßen bei diesen Bedingungen
factors_in_favor: Fahrer fühlt sich nach eigener Einschätzung fit und alert
output.before_you_decide: Schau dir die Umleitung vorher in einer Karten-App oder am Rechner an, damit du die Abbiegungen kennst. Starten erst danach.
safer_options: Strecke inklusive Umleitung am Gerät vorbereiten, erst dann abfahren
Warten, bis die Sicht deutlich besser ist, dann neu entscheiden
Jemanden mit Ortskenntnis der Umleitung fahren lassen, falls das möglich ist
Falls öffentliche Verkehrsmittel oder ein Taxi zu dieser Zeit erreichbar sind, diese als Alternative prüfen
limits: Drive Home hat keine Live-Daten zu Verkehr, Wetter oder Straßenzustand. Diese Einschätzung verwendet nur das, was du angegeben hast. Wenn sich die Bedingungen ändern, bewerte die Fahrt vor der Abfahrt neu.

output.headline: Fahre jetzt nicht los, wenn du sehr müde bist.
output.summary: Die wichtigste Information ist deine aktuelle Müdigkeit. Verschiebe die Fahrt oder nutze eine andere Möglichkeit, nach Hause zu kommen, statt mit starker Müdigkeit zu fahren.
output.main_concern: Du hast angegeben, sehr müde zu sein.
output.before_you_decide: Bewerte die Fahrt erst neu, wenn du wirklich ausgeruht bist und Wachbleiben und Konzentration kein Problem mehr sind.
safer_options: Warte und ruhe dich aus, bevor du die Fahrt neu bewertest.
Bleib dort, wenn das praktikabel ist.
Bitte eine ausgeruhte Person zu fahren.
Nutze Taxi, Fahrdienst, öffentliche Verkehrsmittel oder eine andere verfügbare Alternative.
limits: Drive Home hat keine Live-Daten zu Verkehr, Wetter oder Straßenzustand. Diese Einschätzung verwendet nur das, was du angegeben hast. Wenn sich die Bedingungen ändern, bewerte die Fahrt vor der Abfahrt neu.

input.concern: I caught myself yawning on the walk to the car and it is raining harder than when I arrived.

output.headline: Wait and reassess your alertness before starting — the yawning is the deciding factor here, not the rain.
output.summary: You caught yourself yawning before you even reached the car. Combined with a 45-minute drive through heavy evening traffic in rain on mixed roads, starting while already showing signs of fatigue carries real risk. The rain and traffic you reported can demand sustained attention; tiredness reduces exactly that.
output.main_concern: Yawning on the walk to the car suggests your alertness is already reduced before the drive begins. A 45-minute mixed-road drive in rain and heavy traffic requires sustained attention throughout.
factors_harder: Yawning reported before departure — a sign of reduced alertness, not just mild tiredness
Rain reported at departure, heavier than when you arrived
Heavy traffic on a 45-minute mixed-road route leaves little margin for slower reaction
output.before_you_decide: The decision point is your actual alertness right now. Before starting, establish whether you feel clearly alert and confident you can sustain attention for the full 45 minutes. If you do not feel that way, do not start the drive.
safer_options: Wait somewhere safe and reassess your alertness before deciding to start
If available, have a rested person drive you home instead
If a transit option runs between your location and your destination, consider using it
limits: Drive Home doesn't have live traffic, weather, or road-condition data. This assessment uses only what you reported. If conditions change, reassess before leaving.
